### 2026-10-06 – Today I worked on the schematic and footprint of the PCB of the star boy.

**1.25h**

Today I worked on the schematic and footprint of the PCB of the star boy.

Luckily I remembered using KiCad before and recalled how some of the things worked. Something I found difficult was how the guide mentioned certain things or showed certain things without going in much detail about them, like how certain parts were rotated but it wasn't shown how to, but doing a quick search did answer my questions. I learned about Net Labels, they seem very useful, especially in future complex  plans.

### 2026-10-07 – Today I used the PCB editor in KiCad to arrange and wire the PCB.

**1.25h**

Today I used the PCB editor in KiCad to arrange and wire the PCB.

At first, I was a bit lost as to how to arrange the parts, as the star border I drew was rather pitiful, but I soon realized I could add the image in the guide to help me arrange all the parts.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/xLV9v2yZsf8cQU2Q5GZ9YV3OSKXKe8Gz/2b33e34bcc51674e072becfb7cf4c02ed7085e2c1e7baf8d35cefb30f0ee5556.png)

Thanks to a video explaining borders, I realized how to show the 3d view -->

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/xLV9v2yZsf8cQU2Q5GZ9YV3OSKXKe8Gz/dece38dfaab7572d60eb69bac65061adbbccb54aa1a07182bf5615fc09040d5b.png)

At some point, while doing the wiring, certain parts refused to be wired to parts as shown in the guide image. I can't understand how the image wired itself the way it did. The schematic diagram wants to be wired the way the PCB editor wishes to wire the parts, yet the image somehow did it some other way?

### 2026-10-08 – Today I aim to fix the error that was unexpected.

**0.5h**

Today I aim to fix the error that was unexpected.

Turns out, I missed one connection, as it was pretty hard to see in the image, but the DRC picked it up and I was able to make the connection between my PCB and the image so I fixed that right up.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/xLV9v2yZsf8cQU2Q5GZ9YV3OSKXKe8Gz/d36aed321c6c047daadce72038d145810567b95fcd9edd9923c4c30c3b3021cf.png)

Its the blue wire connection between the two 3.3 V pins.

Just look at how hard it is to see in the image,

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/xLV9v2yZsf8cQU2Q5GZ9YV3OSKXKe8Gz/6ba3c3892de58d3c6bf2765e72fc0955ac6342880affa8a3de82e1fcb89e608b.png)
I suppose this shows just how important and useful the DRC is for everyone.

I spent quite a bit, in fact, too much time trying to find a good image to add to the PCB, and ended up doing this -->
